chapter_theme: The kalivenba turns from Siva to the guru Anandan, the great yogi in a human coat: lord of the gold, silver and stone mountains, the Omkara hill of eight peaks, the man of Kayapuri. Then the guru becomes a warrior who wipes out sect-hatred, tramples the whole order of caste, cuts egoism at the root and routs the mind's and anger's mischief, and finally a horseman: the body is made a horse, the directional wind its cord, the mind its saddle and anger its stirrups, and ridden through the five senses in turiya into the inner fort of bindu and nada, the horse-master who keeps his servants out of hell.
structure_note: 2170 to 2179 praise the guru Anandan by his attributes and places; 2180 to 2187 are the guru as fighter against sects, caste, egoism and the mind's mischief, ending at the drum of silence; 2188 to 2194 are the horse cipher of breath-yoga, each unit adding a piece of harness. Each unit's last word opens the next.

2170.reading: The great yogi who took the shape of a human coat, the Blissful One whose grace runs before even the bull-rider's, honey-thick (2171) on the lotus.
2170.nuance: மானிடச் சட்டை (human coat) treats the guru's body as a garment Siva put on; the poem has moved from God to the man called ஆனந்தன், named in 2171 and 2172 as எங்கள் குரு. யானிடப முந்தும் is obscure; I read இடபம், the bull, so that the guru's grace precedes Siva's own, but the words may be corrupt.

2171.reading: The god hard even for the one on the red lotus (Brahma) to see, the Blissful One who dwells in the body-stain of his servants, our guru (2172).
2171.nuance: அங்கலமத் தேயுறையும் is read as அங்க மலத்தே உறையும், dwelling in the limbs' impurity: the guru lives in the devotees' bodies, impure as they are. A different division gives அங்கலம், a place name, but none is known.

2172.reading: Our guru Anandan, who removes the sorrow of the devotees who love him so that they stand firm, and asks on their behalf; and he is god to the mountains (2173) that are worshipped.
2172.nuance: யாசிக்கும் (begging, asking) makes the guru an intercessor who asks for his disciples; it can also be read as the guru who himself begs, the wandering ascetic. பூசிக்கும் carries into 2173.

2173.reading: He is himself the god to the worshipped mountain of gold, the mountain of silver and the fair mountain of stone, and to the many hills (2174) whose peaks are eight.
2173.nuance: The gold mountain is Meru, the silver Kailasa, the stone perhaps Arunachala, where Siva is a hill; Trikonamalai (Trincomalee), the poet's name-place, is a rock. Making the guru god of these sites turns pilgrimage inward, as 2174 does with the Omkara hill.

2174.reading: He of the firm mountain that is Omkara, whose eight peaks run as the tender shoot of the letter; and firmly (2175) he is the river of Siva's mercy.
2174.nuance: A hill of eight peaks made of the Om-letter: tradition reads the eight as the eight parts of the pranava or the eight-letter mantra of 2160, and the hill as the body with the letter rising in it. The literal sense, a sacred mountain, stands beside this.

2175.reading: He made the river of Siva's mercy flow so that the marks of the servants who seek him are ground to dust; and the servants who do tapas (2176) lose their old deeds.
2175.nuance: சின்னம் (sign, mark) is unclear; the outward marks of the devotees, their sectarian emblems, or their stains may be meant. ஆடும் (dancing) makes the mercy a dancing river.

2176.reading: The servants who do tapas lose their old deeds and reach the flower of his feet; he planted great bliss in the word they utter; and he is (2177) the chaste one in whom they count fullness.
2176.nuance: பேரின்பம் நாட்டினான்: bliss is planted in speech itself, the guru's or the disciple's, not only in silence; 2196 then calls the guru a silent yogi, so both are held.

2177.reading: Known as the steadfast one, with a heart that does not waver, the fair man of the town Kayapuri; and (2178) he of the slight fragrance.
2177.nuance: கற்புடையான் applies a wife's chastity to the guru: unswerving fidelity. காயாபுரி is where the poet later settles (2209); it can be a town's name or, as a coded reading, the body-city (காயம், body). அற்பவிசை carries into 2178.

2178.reading: He of the hill of qualities, fragrant with the honey that flows untouched by bees, caught in a channel; and (2179) in the cut...
2178.nuance: Honey that no bee has touched, dripping of itself, is a figure tradition takes for the nectar that flows in the yogi's head without any outer cause. வாய்ந்தாறைக் கொண்டு is unclear; I read 'taking it in a river'. துண்டத் carries into 2179 and is not clear.

2179.reading: His arm is a distance (?), the ascetic in whom the arrow of the never-resting breath thunders; and the one who takes up the hand (2180) of the servants.
2179.nuance: The unit is damaged: துரமே கரமாய் does not parse, and the following unit is numbered 37, so a unit (36) is lost between them (see source_issues). சரம் can be arrow or breath; ஓயாச் சரமே முழங்கும் as the ceaseless sounding breath fits the horse cipher that follows.

2180.reading: He who took the banner of the ascetic's garb, saying 'the servants' many enemies must be plundered'; and fierce (2181) he wipes out sect-hatred.
2180.nuance: The ascetic's garb is here a war-flag, not a disguise; the enemies to be plundered are inner, as 2181 to 2187 make clear: sect-hatred, caste, egoism, anger, the mind's mischief.

2181.reading: He wiped out the hatred of sects, trampled and ground the whole order of caste underfoot, and cut (2182) egoism at the root.
2181.nuance: சாதிமுறை எல்லாம் குமைய மிதித்து: not a plea for better caste relations but the trampling of the order itself. The verb is the guru's, so caste is destroyed in the disciple by the guru, not by argument.

2182.reading: He cut egoism out by the root and threw it down, and lopped the part that had grown ashamed, so that (2183) its lingering branches were seen.
2182.nuance: ஆணவம் is the first of the three impurities, the soul's self-centredness. நாணமுற்ற பாகம் (the part that had grown ashamed) is obscure; it may be the remnant of ego that survives as shame, or a corrupt phrase.

2183.reading: He flung the branches that still followed so they went like a storm, and to the thick ... the spreading street (2184) and the hall.
2183.nuance: The second line is damaged: அடர்ந்தமக வாகைக்கு அடங்காப் படர்ந்ததெரு does not yield a clear sense; வாகை is the victory-flower, so a victory that does not stay contained may be meant. The image continues the uprooting of egoism as a tree.

2184.reading: In the street and the hall, before the many castes, wearing the holy ash, he trampled falsehood and shouted (2185), scattering the mischief of anger.
2184.nuance: The subject is the guru: he wears the ash in public, where castes are many, and treads lies underfoot. A different reading makes the many castes the ash-wearers who tread in falsehood, which would make the unit an attack on ritual. The first fits the run of 2180 to 2187 better.

2185.reading: He scooped up and scattered the mischief of anger, gathered it, seized the mischief of the mind and shaped it, 'this for you, this for me', and (2186) trampled the mischief of recitation.
2185.nuance: உனக்கென்கென் is read as உனக்கென் எனக்கென், 'yours and mine', the division the mind makes; the guru takes it and remakes it. குறும்பு (mischief, insolence) is repeated through 2185 to 2186 for anger, mind and speech.

2186.reading: He trampled the mischief of recitation, leapt at Death's messenger and drove him off; and (2187) full of the elements he cuts ignorance.
2186.nuance: ஓது குறும்பு is the insolence of mere recitation, book-learning without realisation; the theme returns in 2221 and 2229. Driving off Yama's messenger is the Siddhar claim to conquer death.

2187.reading: He cuts the delusion of ignorance; he is the drum of experience, true knowledge and silence; and the hooded serpent (2188) is his horse.
2187.nuance: வேளத்தான் is unclear; I read a drum (வேள = a kind of drum) sounding knowledge and silence together, but the word may be a place or a title. பைநாகம், the hooded snake, carries into 2188, where the body becomes a horse; the serpent and the horse are both cipher terms for breath or kundalini.

2188.reading: He changed the long body, pressed it and made it a horse, bound it, fitted the bridle that sounds, and (2189) caught the thin cord called the wind of the directions.
2188.nuance: The horse (பரி) is the cipher for breath, and the rider is the வாசியான் of 2194; வாசி means both horse and breath. The long body made into a horse is read by tradition as the breath-body drawn into the practice. கடிவாளம் (bridle) is restraint of the breath; the following units add rope, saddle and stirrups.

2189.reading: Caught by the thin cord called the directional wind, he tightened it with the halter-rope and trained it; unmoving (2190) he set the saddle of mind.
2189.nuance: திசைவாயு, the wind of the directions, is the outgoing breath that scatters toward the senses; it is a thin thread by which the horse is caught, so the breath is both the horse and the rein. குசை is the rope used to halter cattle.

2190.reading: He set and tightened the saddle called mind, fitted the stirrups called anger, and (2191) with heavy snake-binding gait he drove.
2190.nuance: Mind is the saddle and anger the stirrups: neither is discarded; they are harness by which the breath-horse is ridden. This is a different teaching from the suppression of mind and anger; here they become controls.

2191.reading: In the snake-binding gait, the trot and the shaking walk, he let it reach the high sky and drew it in within; and in sorrow (2192) he shattered the mountain of the body.
2191.nuance: நாகபந்தம், சாரி and நடைதுலுக்கு are horse-gaits, read by tradition as modes of breath, the coiled serpent among them. மாகமுற விட்டு உள்ளடக்கி: the breath is sent up to the sky (the crown) and held within, the retention of pranayama. சோகப் carries into 2192 oddly; it may be corrupt.

2192.reading: He shattered the mountain of the body, the eightfold city, leapt over the five senses that slide down, and in turiya (2193) ran to the inner fort.
2192.nuance: புரியட்ட காயம் (புரியட்டகம்) is the subtle body of eight constituents in Siddhanta; it is here a mountain to be broken, not refined. The jump over the senses into turiya is the yogi's passage past waking, dream and sleep.

2193.reading: In turiya he ran to the inner fort called bindu and nada, and in the dance destroyed the boundary of the nadi that withers; and dancing (2194) he is the horse-master.
2193.nuance: The inner fort of bindu-nada is the seat of the subtle sound and light where the breath ends. நாடி வரம்பு அழித்து, destroying the channel's limit, is taken by tradition as the merging of the channels into the sushumna. கூத்து and ஆடியிடும் make the whole ride a dance, recalling Siva's.

2194.reading: He is the horse-master who rose with swelling fury so that the devotees who serve him do not fall into hell; and seeing him they worship (2195).
2194.nuance: வாசியான் closes the cipher: the one who has the horse and the one who has the breath are one word. The fury (சினம்) is the guru's, turned against the servants' enemies of 2180, so anger used as stirrup in 2190 is the guru's own.

links.note: Sivavakkiyar asks what caste is when all water is water and all ornaments one gold; Thirikonar's guru tramples and grinds the whole order of caste underfoot. One argues, the other describes the act, but both deny caste any standing.

Tirumular says that for those who set Nandi firmly in love there is no impurity, no pride and no caste; Thirikonar has the guru wipe out sect-hatred and caste order in the disciple together with egoism in 2182.

The Kural says one who cuts off the pride of 'I' and 'mine' enters a world above the gods'; Thirikonar's guru cuts egoism (ஆணவம்) out by the root. The Siddhar makes the guru the cutter where the Kural leaves it to the renouncer.

Tirumular's two horses, which none knows how to catch until the guru's grace brings them under control, are the two breaths; Thirikonar's body made into a horse, bridled and caught by the cord of the directional wind, is the same cipher, and in both it is the guru who tames it.

Tirumular says to hold the reins of the running horse firmly and asks what use a garb is; Thirikonar's rider sets mind as saddle and anger as stirrups and in 2180 carries the garb only as a war-banner. Both make control of the breath-horse the real discipline.

Pattiragiriyar asks when he will stand unobstructed in the sushumna between ida and pingala; Thirikonar's rider in turiya destroys the boundary of the channel and reaches the inner fort of bindu and nada, the same passage described from the far side.

source_issues: Unit 36 is missing: 2179 is thirikonar:35 and 2180 is thirikonar:37, so two lines of the kalivenba are lost between them and 2179's last word does not connect to 2180.
2179 (துரமே கரமாய்) and 2183 (அடர்ந்தமக வாகைக்கு அடங்காப் படர்ந்ததெரு) do not parse cleanly and are probably corrupt.
